title: Ozi Routing Awareness — Lug creation should announce destination
summary: When Ozi (or AI) creates a lug, it should explicitly route it: LOCAL (this spoke's work), FRAMEWORK (protocol change), or SIGNAL (broadcast to spokes). Current state: lugs created without routing clarity, ambiguous about hub delivery.
description: Session 73: Created 3 lugs for context estimation improvements. Only after creation did we verify routing: (1) signal → hub distribution (framework-wide teaching), (2) epic → local work (Wheelwright Framework's own improvements), (3) task → local work (session item). Should have verified BEFORE creation. Ozi needs routing awareness built in.
root_cause: Lug creation has no routing gate. Ozi doesn't check project identity/boundaries before deciding if work is local vs framework-wide vs broadcast signal.
recommended_implementation: Before lug creation: Load `_project_foundation` + `wheel.node_type` from WAI-State.json
Ask routing question: Is this LOCAL (this spoke's project work) / FRAMEWORK (protocol/schema change affecting all spokes) / SIGNAL (learning to broadcast)?
Add to lug schema: `routed_to` field (enum: local | framework | signal:all-spokes | signal:{spoke-id})
Add `scope_verified_by` field: user confirmation before creation
At closeout: filter lugs by `routed_to` before delivery (local lugs stay, framework/signal lugs copied to hub)
affected_components: Ozi work-queue-monitor (needs routing gate before dispatch)
Wakeup protocol (reporting: which lugs are local vs outbound)
affected_lugs: signal-context-estimation-accuracy-v1 (correctly marked for hub, but implicitly)
learning: Spokes have boundaries. Work discovery should be scope-aware. If Ozi doesn't know 'who am I and what boundaries do I have', it can't properly route work.
next_action: Update Ozi work-queue-monitor skill with routing gate. Extend lug-schema with routing fields.
